raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

```bash
python3 -m pytest test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py -k TestLateLayerTailRequestIndices
```

With `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, every extend forward runs `_build_late_layer_tail_metadata`, which calls `torch.repeat_interleave(req_pool_indices, tail_lens)` with device repeat counts and no `output_size`. PyTorch then copies the total to the host to size the output: one device synchronization per extend forward, although the tail lengths are already on the host (`tail_lens_cpu`).

## Modifications

Adds `_repeat_per_request(values, counts, counts_cpu)`, which passes `output_size=sum(counts_cpu)`, and uses it for the tail request indices.

## Accuracy Tests

The output is the same by construction. `TestLateLayerTailRequestIndices` (new) runs the helper under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")` and checks its values. `test_deepseek_v4.py`: 26 passed (45 subtests) on GB300.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked; it removes one host synchronization per extend forward on the decoder-SWA bounded replay path.

+def _repeat_per_request(values, counts, counts_cpu) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # The total is host-known; without output_size repeat_interleave syncs to size it.
+    return torch.repeat_interleave(
+        values.to(torch.int64), counts.to(torch.int64), output_size=sum(counts_cpu)
+    )

@@ -869,5 +869,26 @@ def test_idle_never_uses_cached_value(self):
         self.assertEqual(out.tolist(), [0, 0])
 
 
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA required")
+class TestLateLayerTailRequestIndices(CustomTestCase):
+    """The tail's per-row request indices are built every extend forward with
+    decoder SWA bounded replay; their size is host-known and must not sync."""
+
+    def test_repeat_per_request_does_not_sync(self):
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.deepseek_v4_backend import _repeat_per_request
+
+        values = torch.tensor([3, 1, 7], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        counts_cpu = [2, 0, 3]
+        counts = torch.tensor(counts_cpu, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+        try:
+            out = _repeat_per_request(values, counts, counts_cpu)
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("default")
+        self.assertEqual(out.dtype, torch.int64)
+        self.assertEqual(out.tolist(), [3, 3, 7, 7, 7])
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
